column1: # Source: Apple Newsroom and apple.com product pages for each A-series chip (per-row quote and source_url)

# Notes: tops is Apple's stated peak Neural Engine rating where basis = stated (A16 and A17 Pro are 'nearly'); A13 basis = derived from two Apple speedup ratios (A12 x 1.2 and A14 / 1.8); A18 Pro basis = secondary (Apple states only 'faster than the previous generation'); A19 Pro has no figure; Apple never states the numeric precision
column2: and the FP16-to-INT8 change at A17 Pro is a secondary-source inference

column5: The new A11 Bionic neural engine is a dual-core design and performs up to 600 billion operations per second for real-time processing.
column7: Corroborated by the M4 release (2024-05): 38 TOPS = '60 times faster than the first Neural Engine in A11 Bionic' (38/60 = 0.63)

column5: A new eight-core design allows it to complete up to 5 trillion operations per second compared to 600 billion in A11 Bionic.
column7: Apple's figure is 'up to', a peak rating

column5: A13 Bionic is built for machine learning, with a faster Neural Engine for real-time photo and video analysis (newsroom). The 8-core Apple-designed Neural Engine is up to 20% faster and uses up to 15% less power (product page).
column7: Apple gave NO ops/s figure for the ANE. The 'over one trillion operations per second' on the same pages refers to the CPU ML accelerators (AMX), not the ANE. 6.0 is derived from Apple's ratios: 5 x 1.2 = 6.0; and the iPhone 12 Pro release says A14 is 11 T with 'an 80 percent increase', giving 11/1.8 = 6.1. Secondary: MacRumors via mjtsai.com/blog/2020/10/13/a14-bionic/ ('6 trillion operations')

column5: A14 Bionic includes a new 16-core Neural Engine that is twice as fast, and capable of performing up to 11 trillion operations per second
column7: Also stated in the iPhone 12 Pro release (apple.com/newsroom/2020/10/apple-introduces-iphone-12-pro-and-iphone-12-pro-max-with-5g/): '16-core Neural Engine ... 11 trillion operations per second ... 80 percent increase in performance'

column5: A new 16-core Neural Engine capable of 15.8 trillion operations per second enables even faster machine learning computations
column7: Same 15.8 T figure Apple later gave for M2

column5: a new 16-core Neural Engine capable of nearly 17 trillion operations per second
column7: Apple says 'nearly' 17 T. Product page (archived 2022-10-20): 'The Neural Engine performs nearly 17 trillion operations per second'

column5: Up to 2x faster Neural Engine performs nearly 35 trillion operations per second with 16 cores
column7: The number appears on the iPhone 15 Pro product page, NOT in the newsroom release, which says only 'the Neural Engine is now up to 2x faster'. Apple says 'nearly' 35 T. Apple states no precision. A 2x jump with an unchanged 16-core count is widely read as an INT8 rating vs FP16 earlier (secondary, e.g. macwelt.de/article/2646535/apple-neural-engine-leistung.html), so the A16 to A17 Pro step is probably not like-for-like

column5: The new 16-core Neural Engine is faster and more efficient than the previous generation (newsroom). New 16-core Neural Engine is faster and more efficient, supercharging Apple Intelligence (product page).
column7: Apple gave NO ops/s figure on the newsroom, product or specs pages. The 35 TOPS comes from secondary sources (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_A18 says 'The same Neural Engine was used in the Apple A17 Pro'; macwelt.de/article/2646535). That conflicts with Apple's 'faster ... than the previous generation', so equal-to-A17 Pro is unverified

column5: The GPU works in tandem with the new 16-core Neural Engine to power AI models ... the 6-core GPU architecture includes Neural Accelerators built into each GPU core
column7: Apple gave NO ANE ops/s figure. Secondary reports of '3x' or '4x peak compute' vs A18 Pro refer to the GPU Neural Accelerators, not the ANE, and they conflict with each other. Do not plot a value
